name: Hello Kitty Swiss Roll
ingredients:
4 eggs
90 g sugar
90 g plain flour
30 ml milk
25 ml vegetable oil
1 tsp vanilla extract
250 ml whipping cream
25 g icing sugar
30 g dark chocolate
40 g white fondant
Red and yellow food colouring
instructions:
Example recipe inspired by the photo; quantities and method are approximate.

1. Heat the oven to 170°C. Line a 25 × 35 cm baking tray with baking paper.
2. Separate the eggs. Whisk the yolks with milk, oil and vanilla, then fold in the flour.
3. Whisk the egg whites, gradually adding the sugar, until stiff peaks form. Gently fold into the yolk mixture.
4. Spread on the tray and bake for 12–15 minutes until springy. Turn onto clean baking paper, peel off the lining and roll loosely while warm. Leave to cool.
5. Whip the cream with icing sugar. Unroll the sponge, spread with most of the cream and roll up again. Chill for 1 hour.
6. Pipe the remaining cream on top. Add fondant ears and a red bow. Use melted chocolate for the eyes and whiskers and yellow fondant for the nose. Draw a face on the cream at the cut end. Keep refrigerated. Makes 6 slices.

name: Strawberry Character Tart
ingredients:
150 g plain flour
75 g cold butter
35 g icing sugar
1 egg yolk
1–2 tbsp cold water
150 ml whipping cream
15 g icing sugar for cream
200 g strawberries
60 g ready-to-roll fondant
Red, green and black food colouring
instructions:
Example recipe inspired by the photo; quantities and method are approximate.

1. Rub the butter into the flour, then mix in 35 g icing sugar. Add the yolk and enough water to form a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
2. Heat the oven to 180°C. Roll out the dough and line four small tart tins. Prick the bases.
3. Line with baking paper and baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the paper and beans, then bake for 5–8 minutes until golden. Cool completely.
4. Whip the cream with 15 g icing sugar and spoon into the shells. Top with sliced strawberries.
5. Colour and shape the fondant into strawberry-shaped cat faces. Add eyes, whiskers and leaves, and place on the tarts just before serving. Makes 4 tarts. Refrigerate after filling.

name: Berry Cheesecake Dessert
ingredients:
120 g digestive biscuits
50 g butter
200 g cream cheese
150 ml whipping cream
40 g icing sugar
1 tsp vanilla extract
100 g strawberries, mashed
100 g raspberries
100 g blueberries
80 g white chocolate
20 g coloured fondant
instructions:
Example recipe inspired by the photo; quantities and method are approximate.

1. Crush the biscuits and stir in melted butter. Press into a small serving dish.
2. Beat cream cheese with icing sugar and vanilla. Whip the cream separately, then fold it into the cheese with the mashed strawberries.
3. Spread over the biscuit base and chill for at least 3 hours.
4. Melt the white chocolate and spoon into small cat-face moulds. Chill until firm and unmould. Use fondant for the facial details and bows.
5. Arrange the chocolate shapes and washed berries over the filling. Keep refrigerated. Makes 4 portions.

name: Pompompurin Butter Cookies
ingredients:
120 g butter, softened
60 g icing sugar
1 egg yolk
180 g plain flour
1 tsp vanilla extract
40 g dark chocolate
instructions:
Example recipe inspired by the photo; quantities and method are approximate.

1. Beat butter and icing sugar until smooth. Mix in egg yolk and vanilla, then stir in flour.
2. Chill the dough for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 170°C and line a baking tray.
3. Roll the dough to 5 mm thick. Cut rounded dog shapes with small ears, arms and feet, joining pieces gently.
4. Bake for 12–15 minutes until the edges are lightly golden. Cool fully on a rack.
5. Melt the chocolate and pipe the hat, eyes, mouth and ear lines. Let the chocolate set. Makes about 12 cookies.

name: Pompompurin Melon Bread
ingredients:
250 g strong bread flour
4 g instant yeast
35 g sugar
1 egg
100 ml milk, lukewarm
25 g butter, softened
3 g salt
100 g plain flour for topping
40 g butter for topping
40 g sugar for topping
1 small egg yolk for topping
30 g dark chocolate
instructions:
Example recipe inspired by the photo; quantities and method are approximate.

1. Mix bread flour, yeast and 35 g sugar. Add egg and milk and knead into a dough. Knead in salt and 25 g butter until smooth. Cover and leave for about 1 hour until doubled.
2. For the topping, beat 40 g butter with 40 g sugar. Mix in the yolk and plain flour. Chill for 30 minutes.
3. Divide the risen dough into 6 balls. Flatten 6 circles of topping and place one over each ball. Score a shallow grid in the topping. Use topping offcuts for ears.
4. Place on a lined tray and leave for 30–40 minutes. Heat the oven to 180°C.
5. Bake for 18–22 minutes until golden and cooked through. Cool completely.
6. Decorate with melted chocolate to make a small hat and face. Makes 6 buns.

name: Bunny Cream Caneles
ingredients:
250 ml milk
25 g butter
1 tsp vanilla extract
100 g sugar
60 g plain flour
1 egg
1 egg yolk
150 ml whipping cream
15 g icing sugar
40 g white chocolate
15 g dark chocolate
Butter for greasing moulds
instructions:
Example recipe inspired by the photo; quantities and method are approximate.

1. Warm milk with butter and vanilla until the butter melts, then leave until lukewarm.
2. Mix sugar and flour in a bowl. Whisk in the egg and yolk, then gradually whisk in the milk. Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours.
3. Heat the oven to 220°C. Butter 6 canelé moulds and fill about three-quarters full with stirred batter.
4. Bake for 15 minutes, reduce to 180°C and bake for another 40–50 minutes until deeply browned. Unmould and cool completely.
5. Whip cream with icing sugar. Cut a cap from each canelé and pipe cream onto the base. Replace the cap loosely.
6. Pipe white chocolate ears onto baking paper and chill. Add ears and dark chocolate facial details to the cream. Makes 6. Keep filled canelés refrigerated. Total time includes the overnight batter rest.

name: White Chocolate Bunny Madeleines
ingredients:
2 eggs
75 g sugar
90 g plain flour
3 g baking powder
80 g butter, melted and cooled
1 tsp vanilla extract
120 g white chocolate
15 g dark chocolate
20 g red and white fondant
Butter for greasing moulds
instructions:
Example recipe inspired by the photo; quantities and method are approximate.

1. Whisk eggs and sugar until pale and thick. Fold in flour and baking powder, then melted butter and vanilla. Chill for 30 minutes.
2. Heat the oven to 190°C. Grease a madeleine tin and spoon batter into each mould, filling about three-quarters full.
3. Bake for 9–12 minutes until risen and golden. Cool completely on a rack.
4. Melt white chocolate. Pipe pairs of bunny ears onto baking paper and chill until firm.
5. Dip the rounded end of each madeleine in the remaining white chocolate. Attach ears while the coating is soft and let it set.
6. Add eyes and a crossed mouth with dark chocolate. Shape small hats from fondant if desired. Makes about 12 madeleines.
